paragraphs.title: The Chosen Servant and His Justice

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Behold my servant... mine elect.”
easy.q: Who is described as God's servant and elect?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have put my spirit upon him.”
easy.q: What has God put upon the servant?

easy.explanation: He will bring forth judgment “to the Gentiles.”
easy.q: For whom will the servant bring forth judgment?

answers: Quietly, without crying out in the street
medium.explanation: He will not cry, lift up, or make his voice heard in the street.
medium.q: How will the servant conduct his ministry?

answers: He protects the weak and does not extinguish hope
medium.explanation: He will not break the bruised reed or quench the smoking flax.
medium.q: What do the bruised reed and smoking flax show about the servant?

medium.explanation: The isles are distant lands that wait for his law.
medium.q: In verse 4, what does “the isles” refer to?

answers: His gentleness prevents him from bringing justice
His gentleness enables him to protect the weak while establishing true justice
His gentleness causes him to hide the law
challenge.explanation: He treats the weak gently while bringing judgment unto truth.
challenge.q: How are the servant's gentleness and his justice related?

answers: Until he has set judgment in the earth
Until people stop hearing his voice
challenge.explanation: He will not fail or be discouraged until judgment is established in the earth.
challenge.q: How long will the servant continue his work?

answers: A compassionate leader who establishes justice and whose law is sought worldwide
challenge.explanation: The passage presents his compassion, justice, and worldwide influence.
challenge.q: Which description best summarizes the servant's role?

paragraphs.title: The Servant's Mission to the Nations

easy.explanation: The Lord is described as the one who created the heavens and spread forth the earth.
easy.q: Who created the heavens and the earth?

answers: A covenant to the people and a light to the Gentiles
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I... will... give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.”
easy.q: What was the servant appointed to be?

easy.explanation: His mission includes opening the eyes of the blind.
easy.q: What will the servant do for the blind?

answers: The Creator is the one who appoints and supports the servant
Creation prevents the servant from acting
medium.explanation: After describing God as Creator, the passage says that He called and held the servant.
medium.q: What is the connection between God's creation and the servant's mission?

medium.explanation: The servant brings prisoners out of prison and darkness.
medium.q: What does “the prison house” represent in verse 7?

answers: To show that He does not share His glory with graven images
To say that prophecy is unnecessary
To announce that the servant will not act
medium.explanation: The Lord declares that His glory and praise belong to Him, not to idols.
medium.q: Why does the Lord emphasize that His glory will not be given to another?

answers: Both describe the creation of the heavens
Both describe a movement from darkness and oppression into freedom and light
Both describe the worship of idols
challenge.explanation: The servant brings sight, light, and freedom to those in darkness and captivity.
challenge.q: What do opening blind eyes and bringing prisoners out of prison have in common?

answers: He will announce them before they come to pass
challenge.explanation: He says, “before they spring forth I tell you of them.”
challenge.q: What does God say about the new things He declares?

answers: They describe a mission affecting both God's people and the nations
They describe two kinds of punishment
challenge.explanation: The servant's mission reaches both the people and the Gentiles.
challenge.q: How are “a covenant of the people” and “a light of the Gentiles” related?

paragraphs.title: The Song of Redemption and God's Victory

answers: To the ends of the earth
easy.explanation: The passage calls for praise “from the end of the earth.”
easy.q: Where are people called to sing a new song?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man.”
easy.q: How is the Lord described when He goes forth to act?

answers: They will be turned back and greatly ashamed
easy.explanation: Those who trust in graven images will be turned back and ashamed.
easy.q: What will happen to those who trust in graven images?

answers: The sea, isles, wilderness, cities, and mountains
medium.explanation: The passage mentions the sea, isles, wilderness, cities, rocks, and mountains.
medium.q: Which places are included among those called to sing?

answers: Let them sing and call out with joy
medium.explanation: The surrounding verses call for singing, praise, and joyful proclamation.
medium.q: What does “let them shout” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: The people are called to declare His praise because of His powerful acts.
medium.q: Why do the nations give glory and praise to the Lord?

answers: Redemption also includes God's powerful action against His enemies
The Lord stops working in the world
The song is meant only for idols
challenge.explanation: The praise is followed by a picture of the Lord acting powerfully against His enemies.
challenge.q: What does the transition from singing to the Lord as a mighty man suggest?

answers: He leads them in unfamiliar paths and turns darkness into light
He sends them to the idols
challenge.explanation: He leads the blind by an unknown way and makes darkness light.
challenge.q: What does the Lord do for those who do not know the way?

answers: The Lord's guidance into light versus the shame of those trusting idols
challenge.explanation: The Lord guides and helps, while idol worshipers are turned back and ashamed.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast at the end of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Blind and Deaf Servant of God

easy.q: To whom is the command “Hear” addressed?

answers: As one who does not properly see or hear
As one who leads the isles
easy.explanation: The servant is called blind and deaf and is said not to observe or hear.
easy.q: How is the servant of God described in this passage?

answers: Magnify the law and make it honourable
easy.explanation: The Lord will “magnify the law, and make it honourable.”
easy.q: What does the Lord desire to do for His righteousness' sake?

answers: The servant sees and hears, but does not observe or listen
The servant cannot see at all and is not called to hear
The servant hears only the idols
medium.explanation: He sees many things but does not observe, and his ears are opened but he does not hear.
medium.q: What contrast is made between seeing and hearing and paying attention?

answers: One expected to be complete or instructed
A person who lives on an island
medium.explanation: The word appears in a description questioning why the servant remains blind despite his position.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “perfect” most nearly mean in the description of the servant?

answers: The Lord is well pleased for His righteousness' sake
The Lord gives him to the idols
medium.explanation: The passage says, “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness' sake.”
medium.q: Despite the criticism of the servant, what is said about the Lord's purpose?

answers: It calls the people to awaken and pay attention, even though they are described as blind and deaf
It proves that the servant has already understood everything
It concerns only the inhabitants of the isles
challenge.explanation: The command urges attention, while the servant is criticized for failing to observe and hear.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the command to the deaf and blind and the description of the servant?

answers: It adds a positive purpose despite the criticism of poor hearing
It removes the need for judgment
It announces that the servant will stop acting
challenge.explanation: After the criticism, the Lord declares that the law will be magnified and honored.
challenge.q: How does the statement about magnifying the law affect the tone of the passage?

answers: Physical sight and hearing are not enough; people must also pay attention and obey
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that seeing and hearing without observing and listening are insufficient.
challenge.q: What central idea emerges from the passage?

paragraphs.title: Israel as the Plundered People and Its Punishment

easy.explanation: The passage says, “this is a people robbed and spoiled.”

answers: They would not walk in God's ways or obey His law
They sang praises to the Lord
They gave light to the nations
easy.explanation: The passage says they sinned and would not walk in God's ways or obey His law.
easy.q: Why did calamity come upon Jacob and Israel?

answers: They did not lay it to heart
easy.explanation: The final verse says that the fire burned them, yet they did not lay it to heart.
easy.q: How did the people respond to their punishment?

answers: They were captured and plundered without a deliverer
They ruled over all the nations
medium.explanation: They were snared, hidden in prison houses, and had none to deliver them.
medium.q: What condition were the people in?

medium.explanation: The people were treated as property taken by robbers.
medium.q: What does “for a spoil” mean in this passage?

answers: Their captivity resulted from refusing God's ways and law
Their punishment was a reward for faithfulness
medium.explanation: The passage identifies their disobedience as the reason they were given for a spoil.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between the people's sin and their punishment?

answers: It calls the people to understand their condition and the reason for their punishment
It announces that no one can hear
It changes the subject to a song of redemption
challenge.explanation: The question challenges the people to listen and understand what has happened.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the question, “Who among you will give ear to this?”

answers: The captivity is presented as a consequence of refusing God's ways and law
The prison houses are places where the law is taught
The passage says there is no connection
challenge.explanation: The people were captured because they would not walk in God's ways or obey His law.
challenge.q: How are the prison houses related to disobedience to God's law?

answers: The people still failed to understand the meaning of their punishment
challenge.explanation: Even after suffering the Lord's anger, the people did not take the lesson to heart.
challenge.q: What does the ending “he laid it not to heart” emphasize?
